facts.question: What is the syntax of each contract between layers?
facts.statement: The contract with Windows is by name: native functions are named with their DLL (for example RegLoadKeyW in advapi32), and registry locations are text paths such as Software\Policies under the machine or user root. Roots accepted by text are HKCU, HKU and HKLM, short or long form. Three lowercase branches (software\policies, software\microsoft\windows\currentversion\policies, system\currentcontrolset\policies) are fixed in code, but only to scope which keys a policy-file difference tracks; other registry paths are still readable and writable.

evidence.shows: Hive load and unload declared with DLL name and wide-string arguments
Typed registry path is split at the first backslash and its root name matched
PolicyKeys lists the three branches, which only limit what ApplyDifference tracks

facts.question: Where is each shape of data defined, in every layer?
facts.statement: Registry data is shaped in code: policy values are typed numeric, string, multi-string or binary and passed through one policy-source interface, with registry, policy file and hive-file implementations. The registry implementation converts unsigned 32/64-bit numbers to the registry's signed form on write and back on read; native structs are defined for token privileges.

evidence.shows: Single interface for reading and writing policy values
RegistryPolicyProxy.SetValue reinterprets unsigned numbers as signed before writing
GetValue reinterprets signed numbers back to unsigned
Two native structures for privilege adjustment

Debug and Release differ only in debug, trace and optimisation flags, and the manifest is embedded in all builds.

facts.question: How is one piece of work carried out, from arrival to response?
facts.statement: One edit: the person opens a policy, the dialog changes an in-memory copy, then File | Save writes it. Only writable sources are saved. Local policy writes the file, then refreshes Windows policy or copies the difference into the registry. Per-user policy refreshes. A policy file is only written to disk; live registry is already applied; an offline user hive applies on close.

evidence.shows: Save writes comments and writable sources, stores choices, shows a message.

Registry, offline hive, null and policy-file sources do different things.
Per-user policy save writes file and refreshes policy.

facts.question: What runs around all incoming work, such as checks every request passes?
facts.statement: Nothing runs around every action: no sign-in, request pipeline or interceptor. The program is attached to an application manifest that Windows reads at launch. When policy sources open and when saving, the program checks and reports whether each source is writable.

evidence.shows: Application manifest is attached to the project.

facts.question: Where do settings and secrets come from, and which live outside the code?
facts.statement: The program keeps its few preferences (last definitions folder, last policy sources, first-run flag) in the current user's registry under a Policy Plus key. It holds no secrets and no configuration file beyond the runtime version pin.

facts.question: How is one piece of work carried out, from arrival to response?
facts.statement: One edit: the person opens a policy, the dialog changes an in-memory copy, then File | Save writes it, plus the comments file, and remembers the chosen sources in the settings key. Only writable sources are saved. Local policy is written to file, then Windows policy is refreshed where Group Policy exists; on Windows Home the difference is copied into the registry and a setting-change message broadcast. Another user's policy folder is written and refreshed. A policy file is only written; the live registry is already applied; an offline user hive applies on close.

facts.question: What runs around all incoming work, such as checks every request passes?
facts.statement: Nothing runs around every action: no sign-in, request pipeline or interceptor. The program is attached to an application manifest that Windows reads at launch; the facts beneath leave its content unstated. When policy sources open and when saving, the program checks and reports whether each source is writable.
